_partNote: Class images for the explorer tiles, rendered at about 74px. Every prompt asks for one bold centered object with a simple silhouette and no fine detail, following the rule in CLAUDE.md: static objects and single simple contacts render correctly, and convergence, immersion, enclosure and internal engagement do not. The seven silhouettes are deliberately far apart — a tapering open lattice tower, a fat reel on its axis, a clamped disc column, a wide finned tank with three tall bushings, a tall narrow cabinet, a horizontal ribbed machine, and a pole with a crossarm — so no two tiles read the same at thumbnail size. Classes IV, V and VII are all boxes in real life, so each is given a different proportion and a different distinguishing feature rather than being drawn as a box.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. Every material, including wire, windings, coils and terminals, is drawn in that same palette. Absolutely no copper, brass, bronze, gold, orange, red, yellow or green anywhere, even where the real object would be that color. Favor open, airy linework with large unfilled light areas over heavy solid gray shading; the drawing should read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Draw the subject as one whole object seen from outside. Do not draw a cutaway, a section view or an exploded assembly.

partPrompts.1: A single steel lattice transmission tower standing alone on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a tapering open framework of straight crossed bracing, wide at the four feet and narrow at the waist, with two horizontal crossarms near the top carrying a few short vertical insulator strings hanging beneath them. Open and skeletal, so the background shows through the bracing. No conductors strung away to the sides, no other towers, no ground detail, no birds.
partPrompts.2: A large cable reel standing upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a wide drum with a big flat circular flange on each side and heavy cable wound in neat visible turns around the barrel between them, with one loose end of cable hanging down and curling on the ground. The two circular flanges are the identifying shape. One reel only, no forklift, no rack, no other cable.
partPrompts.3: A power-electronic valve stack standing upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a straight vertical column built from about eight flat circular disc devices alternating with slightly larger square finned heat sinks, all clamped between a thick flat plate at the top and another at the bottom by four straight tie rods at the corners. Two thin leads leave the base. Rigid, geometric, and clearly a stack of repeated identical layers. No housing, no cabinet, no cables coiled around it.
partPrompts.4: A large oil-filled power transformer standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a wide rectangular tank, distinctly wider than it is tall, with a panel of closely spaced vertical corrugated radiator fins along one long side, and three tall slender insulator bushings standing straight up from the top deck in a row, each ringed with several evenly spaced skirts. A small cylindrical expansion tank lies horizontally along the top edge. One unit only, no fence, no wires, no substation behind it.
partPrompts.5: A single free-standing control cubicle on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a tall narrow rectangular steel cabinet about twice as tall as it is wide, with its front door open to reveal three identical rectangular panel-mounted units stacked in the upper half, each with a small blank display panel and a row of small square buttons, and a plain vertical bundle of wiring running down the lower half. Tall and slim. Not a wide box, no transformer, no fins, no bushings.
partPrompts.6: A large horizontal rotating electrical machine sitting on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a long cylindrical casing lying on its side with evenly spaced circular cooling ribs around its barrel, bolted down onto a heavy rectangular steel bedplate, with a short plain shaft stub projecting from one end and a small rectangular terminal box on top. Exterior view only, not a cutaway. Long, low and cylindrical, with no turbine, no blades, no pipework.
partPrompts.7: A single wooden utility pole standing upright on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a plain round pole with one horizontal crossarm near the top carrying three short vertical insulators, and one small cylindrical transformer can bolted to the pole just below the crossarm with two short leads running up to it. Tall, thin and vertical. One pole only, no wires running off to the sides, no street, no buildings, no ground detail.
